text:
marta: Heads-up, I found a regression in canary that looks tied to structured outputs + tool pauses. p95 decode latency jumped and batch sizes collapsed after the fnframe/stop-token change yesterday. attaching a tiny profile snippet below.

marta: profiler summary: avg_batch_size 12 -> 4, p95_decode 180ms -> 380ms, GPU_util 68% -> 42%, kernel_swap_count 87 -> 310. KV-cache hit-rate for active sessions dropped 0.92 -> 0.73.

marta: snippet:
```
batcher.max_tokens=256
token_budget_target=0.6
queue.policy=latency_pref
kernel_selection: dynamic
observed: frequent kernel swaps on short sequences
```

alex: ugh. do we know if tool calls (function invocations) are causing the batch to flush? is stop-token handling forcing an immediate decode flush?

marta: looks like both. tool pauses cause batches to fragment mid-decode and the stop-token logic triggers early termination paths that evict KV frames. those evictions cause later requests to recompile/select different kernels (small-seq kernel vs long-seq kernel) -> swap thrash.

jin: can we confirm by toggling token_budget_target or disabling the new fnframe fast-path? if avg batch size recovers, that's our culprit.

marta: quick experiment: bumping token_budget_target to 0.85 on one node restored avg_batch_size to ~9 and p95 back to ~200ms. kernel_swap_count dropped to 120. so budget target is definitely a lever.

priya: note though: increasing token_budget_target can increase latency for short critical requests. we should A/B test. also we should fix stop-token handling so it doesn't force KV eviction on structured outputs that will be resumed. maybe mark those frames as resumable.

mike: +1. another angle: queue policy should bias grouping by prefix length and tool-state (calls_pending). current latency_pref policy is too eager to flush. try queue.policy=prefix_grouping, max_batch_delay_ms=12 (was 6) as a smoke test.

marta: tried prefix_grouping + max_batch_delay_ms=12 in canary: avg batch size 11, p95 190ms, but 4% of critical low-latency requests jumped >400ms. those were small single-token queries that we must preserve.

jin: we can add a small exception: if request.is_low_latency_tag then bypass delay. keep prefix_grouping for the rest.

priya: also saw KV-cache churn because structured outputs call small helper functions that append short tokens then return. we should avoid pinning/evicting KV on those transient tool frames. maybe a soft-pin TTL for resumable frames.

marta: agreed. proposed short plan:
1) revert fnframe immediate-evict behavior (temporary) on 1 canary pool.
2) run A/B: prefix_grouping + token_budget_target=0.8 vs control.
3) add tiny perf test with tool-heavy prompt set (10k requests, mix of tool calls + structured outputs).
4) implement soft-pin for resumable frames and run microbench.

devbot: perf-bisect result: commit abc1234 introduced change to fnframe handling (PR #4821). bisect range narrowed to fnframe differ.

alex: thanks bot. who wants to own the revert and A/B?

marta: i'll submit the revert PR and run the canary. jin can set up the A/B and perf harness. priya + mike will design the soft-pin heuristic.

mike: will prototype TTL soft-pin today, share patch in #eng-runtime when ready.

jin: I'll add the tool-heavy corpus to perf infra and schedule the run for tomorrow morning (UTC).

priya: I'll write the checklist for the low-latency exception so we don't regress tail for critical routes.

marta: cool. I'll post canary results in this thread when available. for traceability, here's the trace id for the worst example: trace://r/7f8c9b (included in the profiler bundle).

alex: awesome — thanks. :thumbsup:

marta: Action owners: marta(revert), jin(A/B + harness), mike(soft-pin prototype), priya(low-latency exception). target: verify p95 within 10% of baseline and batch size restored before merging.

marta: ping me if you need the profiling dump or sample request sequences.
